agent_notes: בַר is read as Aramaic 'son' ('Kiss the son'), as KJV/ASV/Webster do; Radak lists son, pure (bar levav) and chosen (beru lakhem ish, 1 Samuel 17:8, in the sense of 'Saul the chosen of the LORD', without a claim about the root), and Meiri prefers 'purity'. I kept 'son' because the 'my son' of verse 7 sets it up. YLT's 'Chosen One' and BBE (which drops the clause) split from it.

STEPBible glosses כִּי as 'if'; I glossed it 'for' (causal after 'lest'). I glossed יִבְעַר as 'it flares' and כִּמְעַט as 'in a moment' (Rashi: ברגע מועט), not 'like a little'. The versions split on kim'at: 'in a moment' (Rashi, ASV, BBE) against 'even a little' (Metzudat David, KJV, YLT). Both are grammatically possible; I follow Rashi because it makes the warning urgent and gives the following 'blessed' its contrast. The commentary presents both.

agent_notes: נָסַכְתִּי: STEPBible 'installed' (נסך II, 'to install, appoint'). The commentators connect it with nesikhim 'princes' (Joshua 13:21, per Radak and Ibn Ezra); the common alternative 'poured (anoint)' is noted in YLT's 'anointed'. I read 'installed' and explain both.

יְלִדְתִּיךָ is a perfect, 'I have begotten you', spoken at the enthronement day. Radak and Meiri read it as adoption or empowerment, not physical birth; I keep the literal 'begotten' and explain the adoption-language of royal ideology in the commentary. I make no claim about later Christian reading, which I left to the reader.

agent_notes: תְּרֹעֵם: the Masoretic vocalization is from רעע 'to break'; the same consonants can be read tir'em from רעה 'shepherd'. YLT ('rule them') and BBE ('ruled by you') reflect that second reading, while the parallel verb tenapetsem 'smash' and the commentators (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Radak, Metzudat David) decide for 'break'. I keep 'break' and mention the alternative in the commentary. Transliteration is now tero'em throughout.

notes.note: Цитаты «RusSynodal» в пакете для PS.2.1–12 не относятся к Псалму 2: это текст из Товита 2:1–10 (сбой выравнивания нумерации). Я сверялся с Синодальным переводом Пс 2 по памяти и не опирался на пакет.
В пакете строка RusSynodal для стихов этого отрывка содержит текст другой книги (Тов 2), поэтому цитаты Синодального перевода взяты из замечаний рецензента и из прежнего перевода, а не из пакета.
